subject.title: active-memory plugin causes session looping when model treats injected context as prompt (2026.7.1)

question: Should Active Memory continue delivering recall through the hidden untrusted prefix for all configured models, or should it gain a supported model/agent policy that suppresses recall when that delivery degrades reply quality?
rationale: The reporter’s corrected trace establishes a quality problem but not a safe universal mechanism: switching trust roles conflicts with the existing security-oriented design, while gating or opt-in changes the feature’s compatibility contract.

options.title: Preserve boundary; define safe suppression
options.body: Keep the hidden untrusted prefix and add a narrowly specified, tested way to skip recall for demonstrably affected agent/model configurations.

options.title: Retain current behavior
options.body: Keep recall available for all configured agents and document that smaller models may visibly acknowledge untrusted context.

options.title: Redesign context projection
options.body: Sponsor a broader runtime-context API that preserves untrusted provenance while making recall less likely to be rendered as conversational content.

recommendation.title: Preserve boundary; define safe suppression
recommendation.body: Keep the hidden untrusted prefix and add a narrowly specified, tested way to skip recall for demonstrably affected agent/model configurations.

likelyOwner.reason: Initial Active Memory feature history is the strongest available ownership signal for choosing its recall-delivery contract.
